q: Which Meta campaigns are wasting money?

checks.what: tool: uses spend plus an outcome metric

answer:
Short answer: several Meta campaigns are spending material budget with few or no attributable orders — that is money likely wasted. Top offenders (last 30 days, scoped to Tilting Heads): campaigns with spend but zero attributed orders, and campaigns with extremely high spend-per-order.

What changed / why it matters
- No orders but spend: DOG TOY CS-10TH-OCT-CS — ₹7,636; TH-073-SMARTSIP-3SEP — ₹4,470; TH-222-WINGBIRD-12OCT — ₹4,207; DOG HARNESS-CTL-12OCT — ₹4,004; TH-270-SIPMATEPRO-19AUG — ₹3,974. These spent without producing attributable orders in the period — immediate candidates to pause or audit.
- Very high cost per order: DOG SHOES-10OCT-CS — spent ₹9,507 for 1 order (spend/order ₹9,507); DOG BEDS-12OCT-CS — ₹8,790 per order; TH-073-SMARTSIP-11OCT — ₹7,947 per order; TH-448-HANDSFREEDOGBELT-PMF-9SEP — ₹6,959 per order; TH-429-TRIMGLOWNAILCUTTER-3SEP — ₹5,547 per order. These are extremely inefficient compared with typical campaign economics.
- Tracking gap: 110 orders have no campaign_name (unattributed) in the same window — this can hide where spend is actually converting and inflate apparent waste.

Worth checking: pause or cap spend on the zero-conversion campaigns, and immediately check campaign → tracking / tagging and the unattributed orders (110) before broader cuts.

Basis & scope: ad spend = paid_media (report_date); orders = orders with touchpoints (order_date); brand default = Tilting Heads. 

Period: 2026-09-16..2026-10-15 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-16
